info.name: 3PL Automation - Logic Apps
info.description:
Requests for the 5 Request-triggered Logic Apps (Standard) workflows in three3pllogicapp:
- btp-config-publish
- mulesoft-config-generation
- mulesoft-config-publish
- solace-config-generation
- solace-config-publish

Each workflow has a single `When_a_HTTP_request_is_received` trigger that calls one local .NET function (see lib/custom/*/function.json) and returns its output as the HTTP response body.

**Local testing (default):** run the project with `func host start` (or F5 in VS Code with the Logic Apps Standard extension). The `baseUrl` collection variable defaults to `http://localhost:7071`, and no signature is required locally.

**Deployed/Azure testing:** set `baseUrl` to `https://<your-logic-app-name>.azurewebsites.net`, then enable the disabled `sv`/`sp`/`sig` query params on the request (values come from the workflow's Callback URL in the Azure Portal, or `az rest`/`az logicapp` callback-url APIs) since Standard Logic App HTTP triggers are SAS-signed when hosted in Azure.

Note: `githubToken` for the mulesoft/solace publish workflows and TriggerBtpDeployment's `githubToken` are both read from the `githubToken` app setting on the server side (`appsetting('githubToken')`), not from the request body, so they are intentionally omitted from these request bodies.

request.description: Fans out to btp-config-publish, mulesoft-config-generation→mulesoft-config-publish, and solace-config-generation→solace-config-publish in parallel, each wrapped in its own Scope (Scope-BTP/Scope-MuleSoft/Scope-Solace) inside an outer Scope-Try/Scope-Catch. Do NOT send appYaml/devYaml/tstYaml/prodYaml under mulesoft.publish or solaceConfigJson under solace.publish — the orchestrator wires those in itself from the matching generate step's output (body('Invoke_MuleSoft_Config_Generation') / body('Invoke_Solace_Config_Generation')). Only send the fields each generate/publish step actually needs from the caller (csvContent, repo/branch/path, commitMessage). On success returns 200 with all 5 child outputs nested under btp/mulesoft/solace; on any child failure returns 500 with per-branch failure detail (result('Scope-Try') plus each domain's own result()).

Triggers a GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch (btp-Api-management-deploy.yml) via TriggerBtpDeployment. All body fields fall back to defaults baked into btp-config-publish/workflow.json if omitted; githubToken always comes from the server-side `githubToken` app setting.

request.description: Builds app/dev/tst/prod.yaml from a MuleSoft NAV onboarding requirements CSV (long format, one row per RowType: Environment/TransactionType/MessageType/SourceDestination/UomMapping). Set updateExisting=true and populate existingAppYaml/existingDevYaml/existingTstYaml/existingProdYaml to merge incrementally instead of building fresh. See MuleSoftCsvParser.cs for the full column reference.

request.description: Commits non-blank appYaml/devYaml/tstYaml/prodYaml content to a GitHub feature branch under filePathPrefix (creating the branch from baseBranch if needed). Normally chained after 'MuleSoft Config Generation' in the real pipeline, but can be called standalone for testing. githubToken is not accepted in the body here (Logic App reads it from the githubToken app setting).

Generates Solace onboarding config JSON from a CSV batch (multiple Brand/Env/SystemName/ThreePLCode records per call, unlike MuleSoft's single-record CSV). Body defaults to the same sample CSV baked into solace-config-generation/workflow.json's coalesce() default. Can be omitted entirely to exercise that default.

Commits solaceConfigJson to a GitHub feature branch at filePath (creating the branch from baseBranch if needed). Normally chained after 'Solace Config Generation'; replace solaceConfigJson with real output from that call for an end-to-end test. githubToken is not accepted in the body here (Logic App reads it from the githubToken app setting).
